clue.text: Piece of hip hop's broadcast round backyard

indicators.note: something broadcast goes out over the air, so we want a word that sounds like the clue's word when spoken

parts.note: hip hop is rap music; its possessive is said the same as these letters
O is round in shape
YD, the abbreviation for yard, written back to front

explanation.surface: A hip hop track gets played out across someone's back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The backyard is read as an instruction: the short form of yard, turned back. The sound-alike piece is respelt with an H to match the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a musical composition, so it is a piece in the sense of a work of music.

clue.text: Bug scuttled over large beast

parts.note: to scuttle is to run quickly

indicators.note: in a down clue, over suggests turning a word upside down, so it reads upward

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

explanation.surface: An insect hurried across a big animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, and something that rankles keeps irritating.

clue.text: Secondary navigation by way of train lines gets birds home

indicators.note: secondary points at the item in second place, here a single letter of the next word

parts.note: the second letter of navigation
via means by way of
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Routing a train along branch lines is how pigeons reach their loft.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is an enclosure where birds are kept, so it serves as their home.

clue.text: TV show: very much a quiet time after work

indicators.note: after places the period of time behind the word for work in the build

parts.note: so means very much, as in 'so tired'
taken as written
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
OP is short for opus, a work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A television programme presented as a calm evening after the working day.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial drama broadcast on television.

clue.text: Police rise high in patriots cruel tyranny

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the following word
cruel treatment knocks things out of shape, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for high

explanation.surface: Police officers climb the ranks among nationalists under a brutal regime.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyranny is absolute and oppressive rule, which a dictatorship is by nature.

clue.text: Thief taking dresser without key?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a whimsical word for one who robes, or dresses, someone
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A burglar makes off with a sideboard without needing a key.
explanation.walkthrough: The dresser is not furniture but a made-up 'one who robes', which the question mark excuses.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is someone who steals, which is what a thief does.

clue.text: Give thoughts on pie ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients are mixed together, so the letters before it get stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is asked for their views on what goes into a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to express an opinion, which is giving your thoughts.

clue.text: Bear cub disrupted English party cooking food outdoors

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A young bear wrecks a garden party where food is being grilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is a social gathering where food is grilled in the open air.

clue.text: Record disheartened Rorke's Drift soldiers coming back up

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart is removed, leaving only the outside letters of the name

parts.note: the first and last letters of Rorke
the drift of an argument is its gist

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming back up means reading the letters bottom to top

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Recalls the 1879 battle of Rorke's Drift, where a small British garrison held off a Zulu army.
explanation.walkthrough: Rorke's Drift reads as a single place name, but splits into two pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official record or list, and to register is to record.

clue.text: One son's in slight hint of trouble

indicators.note: in tells us to put the first pieces inside the word for a faint suggestion

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle shade or hint
S is the abbreviation for son; the 's is read as 'is'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boy shows a faint sign that he is about to misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is a source of annoyance or bother, which is what trouble can mean.

clue.text: Derrick's putting grease on machinery

indicators.note: putting one thing on another places it in front when written across

parts.note: oil is a lubricant, as grease is
a rig is an apparatus or set of equipment

explanation.surface: A man called Derrick is lubricating some machines.
explanation.walkthrough: Derrick looks like a man's name, but it is the tower used over a well.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is the framework over an oil well, and an oil rig carries one.

clue.text: Lady pursuing good times has strange slant on principles

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the title for a lady comes after the good times

parts.note: fun is enjoyment

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the ordinary, so the letters next to it are jumbled

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeking woman has odd views about ethics.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamentals are the basic rules or truths on which something rests, as principles are.

clue.text: Cut short heavy old slow movement

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off the word that follows

parts.note: large means big or heavy
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An old, heavy piece of music is trimmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the Italian tempo marking for very slow, and names a movement played that way.

clue.text: Brains and a pretty head?

parts.note: taken as written
cute means pretty
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone has both intelligence and good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: The head is not a face but a headland: NESS appears in place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuteness is sharpness of mind, which is what having brains means.

clue.text: Innate tendency to censure and abuse

indicators.note: abuse means ill treatment, which here bends the letters into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is naturally inclined to criticise and insult people.
explanation.definitionFit: Second nature is a habit so ingrained it feels inborn, an instinctive tendency.

clue.text: Prisoner jumping from a soft-top car can be stopped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: jumping from means leaping out, so those letters leave the word for the car

parts.note: a convertible is a car with a folding roof
con is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: A convict leaps out of an open-topped car to escape, which might be prevented.
explanation.definitionFit: Avertible means able to be averted, that is prevented or turned aside.

clue.text: Determined Hebridean island's to harbour longship

indicators.note: to harbour is to give shelter, so the island holds a letter inside it

parts.note: Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
L for long, plus SS for steamship

explanation.surface: A Viking longship is sheltered by a resolute Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Longship splits into 'long' and 'ship'; only the L goes inside the island, with the ship's letters tacked on after, so the 's here is just 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tireless never flags, which shows they are determined.

clue.text: Cultured university guy's besieged by journalists

indicators.note: besieged by means surrounded, so the first pair is enclosed by the others

parts.note: ED is short for editor; the plural supplies two of them
U is the abbreviation for university
cat is old slang for a man or guy
the second editor closing the siege

explanation.surface: A graduate is hounded by reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: Journalists here are two EDs, one on each side; the 's of guy's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educated is well schooled and refined, which is what cultured means.

clue.text: Unseasonal warmth brings forth sub-continental adder

parts.note: India is the subcontinent
an adder is one who adds, a summer

explanation.surface: A warm spell produces a snake from South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The adder is not a snake but someone who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian summer is a spell of warm weather in autumn, when it is out of season.

clue.text: Scheme to get unknowns into rising NY team

indicators.note: into tells us to put the letters for unknowns inside the other word
in a down clue, rising means reading the team's name upward

parts.note: the New York Mets are a baseball team
Y is an algebraic unknown; two of them

explanation.surface: A plan to sign unknown players for an up-and-coming New York side.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method or plan, which is what a scheme is.

clue.text: Drink to Queen's name in Hull

indicators.note: in places the monarch and the name inside the word for a husk

parts.note: a pod is the hull of a pea or bean
ER is Elizabeth Regina; the 's is 'has'
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A loyal toast to the monarch given in the city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the Yorkshire city, but it is the husk of a pea.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit, a drink.

clue.text: Cousin Rex organised trip

indicators.note: organised means arranged anew, so the letters of the two words are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A relative called Rex arranged an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: An excursion is a short journey made for pleasure, which is a trip.

clue.text: Wash out some swimwear in sea water

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, a run of letters inside the phrase

parts.note: the run of letters spans the end of swimwear, the word in, and the start of sea

explanation.surface: Advice to rinse your swimming costume in the sea after a swim.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse something is to wash it out with clean water.

clue.text: My turn to cut the herb for cooking

indicators.note: to cut means to slice into, so the pair goes into the other word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turn means the possessive word is spun round to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook announces it is their turn to chop the herbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb widely used in cooking.

clue.text: Reach out to former nurse

parts.note: ex means former
to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Making contact again with a woman who used to be a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to stretch out, as one does when reaching out an arm.

clue.text: Holy man's not returned from ramble

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher; the 's is 'has'

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman has not come back from a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramble looks like a walk, but it is the verb for talking on and on; to rabbit on is British slang for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is to talk at length aimlessly, which is to ramble in speech.

clue.text: Dad's lost bearings, being upset

indicators.note: lost suggests being all at sea, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N and E are compass bearings, north and east

explanation.surface: A father is unhappy at having lost his way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost bearings' reads as one phrase about direction, but 'lost' is the instruction and 'bearings' only supplies two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To sadden someone is to make them unhappy, which is to upset them.

clue.text: Respected heads of European states reportedly co-operated

indicators.note: heads of points to the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of European and states

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so we want a word that sounds like one meaning the clue's word

parts.note: people who co-operated teamed up; it sounds like a word for swarmed

explanation.surface: European leaders are said to have worked well together and earned respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone esteemed is highly regarded, which is what respected means.
